about.title: About
about.body:
A small technical notebook. Mostly notes to my future self on software, systems, and the web, written in plain HTML.

No trackers, no frameworks, no build step. Just text that loads fast and lasts.

posts.title: Why static sites still win
posts.summary: No build step, no server to patch, no database to lose. A short case for keeping things plain.
posts.body:
A static site is just files. GitHub Pages serves them straight from a repository, so there is nothing to keep running and nothing to patch at 2 a.m.

The best infrastructure is the infrastructure you do not have to operate.

What you give up

Dynamic features: comments, search, personalization. Most of those have static or third-party answers, and most blogs never needed them.

What you get back

Speed, security, and longevity. A folder of HTML from 2010 still opens today. That is not true of most content management systems.

posts.title: Hello, world
posts.summary: Starting a small technical notebook. Here is what to expect.
posts.body:
This is the first post. The goal is simple: a fast, readable place to write down things I learn.

Expect short pieces on tooling, the web platform, and the occasional debugging war story. When code helps, it will look like this:

curl -s https://tech.livive.net | wc -c

That is the whole page, tags and all. Keeping it small is the point.
